hypotheses.justification:
The statement never mentions `MeasurableSpace (R i)` or `BorelSpace (R i)`. The only measurable structure it uses is the separate `[MeasurableSpace (∀ i, R i)ˣ]` and `[BorelSpace (∀ i, R i)ˣ]`. `localShellProbability` is a `def`, so it only takes the section variables its body uses. Its body is `orbitContainmentProbability ν L (productDVRShell_nonempty R k).choose`, which needs no measurable structure on `R i`. `modelUnitProbability` and `modelLocalModule` don't need one either. The conclusion is therefore independent of any `MeasurableSpace (R i)`.

The proof uses `BorelSpace (R i)` in one place only. It calls `actual_containment_eq_model_orbit` with `R := ∀ i, R i`, which needs `MeasurableSpace` and `BorelSpace` on the product. These come from the instance `Pi.borelSpace`, which needs `Countable ι` (from `Fintype ι`), `SecondCountableTopology (R i)` and `BorelSpace (R i)`.

Without the hypothesis, start the proof with `letI : ∀ i, MeasurableSpace (R i) := fun i => borel (R i)` and `haveI : ∀ i, BorelSpace (R i) := fun i => ⟨rfl⟩`. The rest of the proof is unchanged, because the other lemmas used (`productDVRShell_*`, `orbitContainmentProbability_smul`, `modelUnitProbability_isProbability`, `modelUnitProbability_isHaar`) don't depend on a measurable space on `R i`. The statement doesn't depend on the chosen instance, so it stays true and provable.

The companion binder `[∀ i, MeasurableSpace (R i)]` is mentioned by the `BorelSpace` binder, so it can only be dropped together with it. Once `BorelSpace` is dropped it is also unused and can be removed. I did not check the other instances: `SecondCountableTopology (R i)` and `Fintype ι` look needed, because they feed `Pi.borelSpace` and the second-countability of the product.
